name: Superwhisper
tagline: AI dictation for Mac that turns speech into text anywhere

pricing.notes: Official docs/checkout checked 2026-07-30; Pro monthly listed at $8.49, annual $84.99, lifetime $249.99.
pricing.freeTier: A free version covers basic dictation; Pro adds unlimited cloud and local models.

verdictSummary: A push-to-talk recorder that transcribes and pastes text into the active app is very buildable for one person, especially on macOS.
coreLoopDIY: Bind a hotkey, capture microphone audio, transcribe with Whisper or speech API, optionally rewrite with an LLM, and paste into the active field.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for the low-friction menu-bar experience and dictation profiles.

priorArt.name: whisper.cpp
priorArt.desc: Local transcription engine that makes a simple dictation clone realistic.

alternatives.name: FluidVoice
alternatives.desc: Fast Mac dictation with local cleanup; even the fancy part stays on the machine.

alternatives.name: Handy
alternatives.desc: Press a key, talk and get plain text in the app you were already using. No cleanup magic, no invoice.

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: Hold a key, talk and get cleaned text at the cursor; the local meeting recorder comes along for free.

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: A cross-platform hotkey-to-cursor app with local models, cleanup, history and meeting capture.

alternatives.name: Spokenly
alternatives.desc: Unlimited local dictation behind a polished installer; cloud convenience is the bit it charges for.

alternatives.name: TypeNo
alternatives.desc: Control, talk, Control, paste. It has no settings because there is nothing to upsell.

alternatives.name: Voicebox
alternatives.desc: Voice cloning studio attached to a global dictation hotkey; overkill, free overkill.

alternatives.name: Voquill
alternatives.desc: System-wide dictation, local Whisper, cleanup and a glossary; cloud convenience is the paid part.

rejectedAlternatives.name: VoiceInk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The code is open, but the usable download is a trial; the free path is compiling it yourself in Xcode.

notes: Strong yes and very on-brand for vibecoding: small utility, obvious primitives, high subscription annoyance.
prompt:
Build me a push-to-talk dictation tool for macOS to replace Superwhisper. Requirements:

- A global hotkey (default: hold right Option) records my mic while held, stops on
  release. A small Swift menu bar app or a Hammerspoon script, pick the simpler to
  ship.
- Record with ffmpeg (avfoundation) to a temp wav, transcribe locally with whisper.cpp
  (small.en by default, model path in a config file). Works fully offline, no cloud
  speech APIs.
- Paste the result into whatever field has focus (simulate Cmd+V via CGEvent or
  osascript, then restore my previous clipboard).
- Optional cleanup mode on a second hotkey: send the transcript to an LLM (key in
  .env) to fix punctuation and drop filler words, then paste. If no key is set, this
  mode just does a plain paste.
- Menu bar icon shows idle/recording/transcribing; clicking it lists the last 10
  transcripts with copy buttons.
- Append every transcript to ~/Dictation/YYYY-MM.md with a timestamp, and delete the
  audio after transcription. No accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: per-app presets and custom vocabulary tuning. One good general mode.
- README: mic + accessibility permissions to grant, how to download the whisper
  model, and a note that the first run will trigger macOS permission prompts.
